req_desc:
Deployment and health
The app serves from its run manifest on `0.0.0.0` at `APP_PUBLIC_PORT`, answers `GET /api/health` with `200` and the health body the API section defines, including its `identity` key, and answers every page and API route whatever host name the request carries.

Server-rendered surfaces
Every staff surface and both public surfaces answer their own address with their headings, copy and data already in the first HTML response, and every staff route opened without a session redirects to `/login`.

Sign in
`POST /api/auth/login` exchanges a seeded work email and passphrase with the identity provider server-side and returns the app's own opaque `access_token`, and `GET /api/auth/me` answers `{ id, email, name, role }` with the role the seed gave that account.

Sign out
`Sign out` and `POST /api/auth/logout` end the session server-side, so the revoked token is refused on every later read and write.

Credential refusal and lockout
Every failed sign-in gets the same status and byte-identical body whether or not the email belongs to an account, and the fifth failure for one trimmed, lower-cased email within the lockout window locks that email out, as qualified in Business rules.

Sign-in redirects
A staff route opened without a session redirects to `/login?next=<PATH>`, `next` is honoured only for a same-origin path beginning with a single `/`, and the public wall and plaque never redirect.

Role permissions and draft privacy
Every write is checked server-side against the role table and refused with `403` when the role may not act, every signed-in role reads every staff surface, and a maker naming another maker's draft on any route gets `404`.

Auditor read-only
An `auditor` opens every piece by its id but is refused every write with `403`, its own preferences being the one exception, and no refused write changes anything stored.

Own-piece rule
The account that created a piece may not record either review on it, clear it or publish it, refused with `403` and the own-piece message, and the refusal writes nothing.

Second-reviewer rule
The account that recorded a piece's licence review may not record its accessibility review, refused with `403` and the second-reviewer message, while a different accessibility reviewer may.

Citation checks
Submitting a piece that cites no object, or cites an unusable object, is refused on `object_ids` with one line per offending object naming one of the three pinned reasons.

Duplicate acknowledgement
A licence review cannot pass while any flagged duplicate of a cited object is unacknowledged in the current review round, and each acknowledgement is stored once with who made it, for which piece and when.

Legal steps
A piece moves only along the rows of the state table, each successful step raising `version` and appending exactly one audit entry, with `Import pack` as the one stated exception that creates pieces directly in a state.

Illegal steps
Any step or `action` value outside the state table is refused with `409` and the illegal-step message, leaving the piece and the audit trail unchanged.

Revision resets the round
Revising a piece back to `draft` is the owning maker's step alone and discards both review records and every duplicate acknowledgement for that piece, so the next round starts from nothing.

Version conflicts
A write carrying a stale `version` answers `409` with the current piece, and two decisions sent from one version, including a licence and an accessibility review at the same moment, end in exactly one success and one conflict.

Field rules
Titles, summaries, fees and reasons outside their ranges are refused on their field and store nothing, and every money value is held as a whole number of cents.

Clearance queue
`/` lists every piece this account may see with its state chip and both review marks, counts the nine states over those pieces, searches, sorts, pages at the account's `Rows per page` and states the result line.

Needs my decision
The `Needs my decision` filter answers each role exactly the pieces Business rules gives it to decide, and nothing for an auditor.

Decision rail
The piece desk offers only the actions this account may take from this state, leaving every other action absent rather than disabled, and `New piece` is rendered only for a maker.

Catalogue walk
`GET /api/objects` pages by cursor against a seed so a full walk returns every matching object exactly once before it reports `wrap`, the same seed and cursor always rebuild the same board, and a new seed only reorders it.

Catalogue board
`/catalogue` draws each object at its own stored proportions between 48 and 220 pixels on its longer side, as a control named by its title that lifts and reveals its artist and licence on hover or focus.

Duplicate check
`GET /api/objects/{id}/similar` scores each pair from 0 to 100, the same in both directions and on every call, ordered highest first then by ascending id, and the object detail lists those objects below its record.

Featured schedule
At most one piece holds any UTC calendar day even when two bookings arrive at once, a taken day is refused with `409` and a past day is refused, as Business rules sets out.

Plaque visitor count
A plaque raises its booked day's visitor count by one the first time it is opened in a browsing session, and the schedule's `Today` panel states that count.

Public wall
`/wall` needs no session and shows only published pieces, most recently published first, as cards linking to `/wall/<PIECE_ID>`, which answers 404 unless that piece is published.

Plaque
The plaque gives each cited object's title, artist, licence name and licence address under `Sources`, the maker under `Credits`, and ends with the cleared line naming the date and the lead.

Committed budget
Committed is the summed fee of every piece in `cleared`, `scheduled` or `published` whose `cleared_at` falls in the quarter, and a clear that would take committed above the budget is refused with `409` naming the exact overspend, even when two clears arrive at once.

Fee adjustment and reset
A lead adjusts a fee through the number field, the `x10`, `x100` and `x1,000` buttons and `Apply`, and `Reset quarter` asks for confirmation before returning every fee in the quarter to its submitted value, neither ever taking committed above the budget.

Audit trail
The trail is append-only, filters by piece, actor, to-state and date range, pages at the account's `Rows per page`, and `Export CSV` downloads the filtered rows quoted and made spreadsheet-safe as the CSV rules state.

Preferences
Each account's `Rows per page`, `Date display` and `High contrast` default to 50, `relative` and off, save at once into one row per account, and survive signing out and back in.

Clearance pack
`Export pack` returns every piece as one document, and `Import pack` applies a clean pack completely or refuses a bad one with its pinned message while writing nothing at all.

Persistence
Every piece, review, acknowledgement, booking, fee, session and audit entry lives in `postgres` and survives a reload, a restart and the seed path running again unchanged.

Responsive layout
The queue becomes stacked cards at or below 600 pixels, the wall steps from one to four columns at 600, 800 and 1300 pixels, the queue shows `Fee` and `Updated` above 1000 pixels, and nothing scrolls horizontally from 320 pixels up.

Accessibility
Pages meet WCAG 2.2 AA, a whole review including its dialog can be done by keyboard alone with a visible focus ring on every control, dialogs trap focus, close on `Escape` and return focus, every drawn cut-out and icon-only control carries its published name, and no status rests on colour alone.

Motion
The decision stamp and the wall card entry are browser-native animations with the timings Motion and effects gives, and under the reduced-motion setting both become instant with all content kept.

Self-contained build
The app ships its own stylesheet with no utility-class framework or fingerprint, draws every picture, links nowhere off-site, and its pages make no browser or asset request to another host.

Public chrome
The public pages carry the tagline, the footer line and the count of pieces whose first clearing fell on the current UTC day, which never moves on an unschedule or a withdrawal.

List failures
A list whose request fails shows the list-failure message with a `Try again` control while the rest of the page keeps working.

Surface copy
Every pinned label, empty-state sentence, count line and pager line appears on the surface this brief places it on.

Paper and sheets
The light field is a near-white paper neutral with every card, panel and dialog on pure white above it, near-black ink for primary text and a mid cool neutral for secondary text.

Colour by meaning
One mid blue means press here, one green means passed or cleared, one light vivid orange means waiting or flagged and fields the `Shuffle` button, one red means refused or failed, and a warm cream field is reserved for pieces on the public wall.

Two type roles
Interface labels, table text and prose use a plain system sans, and every identifier, count, money amount and timestamp uses a system monospace with tabular numerals.

Staff header
Every staff page carries one white header bar above a hairline with `Clearhouse` linking to `/` beside the centre's name, the five surface links, the signed-in name, a role chip and `Sign out`.

Density and composition
The queue is a dense comparison table beside a narrow sidebar, the wall is generous with large cards and wide gutters, and the plaque is one narrow reading column.

Drawn pictures and icons
Every cut-out and cover is drawn by the app from stored records, and every icon is a thin unfilled line drawing from one set.

High contrast
The `High contrast` preference keeps the same light layout while deepening hairlines, well edges, secondary text and status tints.

Designed empty and placeholder states
Empty lists show their pinned sentence where the rows or cards would stand, and loading lists show grey placeholders shaped like the rows or cards they await.

Identity outage
While the identity provider is unreachable the app still starts and stays healthy, sign-in answers `503` without counting toward lockout, existing sessions keep working, and sign-in recovers with no restart once the provider returns.

Only published fields
A JSON write body carrying any key outside its endpoint's published fields is refused with `400` on the first such key and stores nothing, the clearance pack excepted.

Refusal order
A request with several faults is answered by the first failing check in the one published refusal order.
`/app/run.json` is valid JSON carrying `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"` and string `install`, `build` and a non-empty foreground `serve`.
`/app/USER_README.md` lists the six seeded emails, their roles and the passphrase `deku-demo-pw-2026`.
Empty `.browser_screenshots/` and `.downloads/` directories exist at the app root.

`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names every shipped package with its licence; shipped packages means the production dependency tree, everything the `install` command installs including transitive dependencies (the lockfile's non-dev group), and no test or development tool.
Every shipped package carries one of MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC, PSF-2.0, MPL-2.0 or LGPL-3.0-or-later.
No shipped package is a client for any datastore other than PostgreSQL, and the app writes no database file of its own.
The provided service configuration and the realm's client settings are left untouched.
